title: Quasar AI - POC scoping: latency & throughput SLOs

Customer to provide representative prompt set, traffic profile, and sample payloads by 2027-05-09
Schedule 1-hr deep-dive benchmark review with infra stakeholders week of 2027-05-17
Agree final POC success criteria and sign SOW to start reserved capacity pilot
action_items: Jordan Lee - Share pricing and Dedicated capacity options - 2027-05-10
Priya Kapoor - Provide benchmark harness, Locust scripts, and config (batching, seq len dist) - 2027-05-11

Redwood to run synthetic and production-shadow benchmarks; customer to provide prompts and traffic pattern. 4-week POC timeline proposed with clear success criteria and measurement plan.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-06 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Kapoor, Ethan Morales, Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill, Sofia Park

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. this is jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya and I are here to scope the poc for latency and throughput SLOs.
[00:12] Ethan Morales: yeah thanks, um quick intros - i'm ethan, cto, maya is our ml eng who owns inference, liam is infra, sofia is product.
[00:20] Priya Kapoor: great - quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, TTFT vs TPOT definitions, target p95/p99, and measurement plan and timeline. sound good?
[00:30] Maya Chen: yes. to start, our main user-facing metric is time to first token, we want interactive responses for our code-assist product. currently using an inference cluster on premise and average TTFT is around 650ms p95 during peak which is too high.
[00:47] Jordan Lee: got it. and what QPS are you seeing in peak?
[00:50] Liam O'Neill: peak single-digit qps per model right now, but we have bursts to ~40 qps across tenants. bursts last 10-20s usually.
[00:59] Sofia Park: and our target is to make the product feel snappy - internal target p95 TTFT < 200ms, p99 < 400ms. is that realistic?
[01:10] Priya Kapoor: ok, quick definition check so we're aligned: TTFT = time from request accepted to the first token emitted by the model. TPOT = time per token after first token streaming begins. For some use cases TPOT matters more (long streaming outputs) and for others TTFT dominates (short responses).
[01:28] Ethan Morales: we care about both but first token is most important because responses are usually short - mean tokens ~12, 90th ~40.
[01:36] Jordan Lee: perfect context. rough targets we often propose for interactive apps on Dedicated: TTFT p95 <= 150-250ms and p99 <= 300-500ms depending on model and quantization. TPOT p95 typically 8-20ms per token with GPU-backed serving.
[01:52] Maya Chen: that seems in line; curious about measurement differences - how do you measure TTFT? we have seen different numbers between synthetic and prod.
[01:59] Priya Kapoor: good question - measurement plan we recommend three phases:
[02:02] Priya Kapoor: 1) Synthetic baseline: controlled load generator (we use Locust + Redwood benchmark harness) to measure TTFT/TPOT with pinned model, seq length distribution, and batching turned off and then with realistic batching.
[02:14] Priya Kapoor: 2) Production shadowing: mirror a percentage of live traffic (no external side effects) to Redwood hosted endpoints to measure true tail behavior and KV cache effectiveness.
[02:24] Priya Kapoor: 3) Canary + longitudinal: run canary in prod or Dedicated pilot for 1-2 weeks to capture real user patterns and tails.
[02:31] Ethan Morales: ok that makes sense. for synthetic tests, we need config details - batch sizes, max seq len, model variants (FP16, int8).
[02:39] Jordan Lee: for the poc we recommend running three model variants: full fp16, 8-bit quantized, and a smaller distilled model as fallback. measure TTFT and TPOT at p50/p95/p99 for each. batch size sweep: 1, 2, 4, 8 and continuous batching window 10-50ms to match interactive latency goals.
[02:55] Maya Chen: our current seq len distribution: median 30, 95th 120. code completions are often short but some diffs are long.
[03:03] Priya Kapoor: noted - that will affect KV cache effectiveness and memory. KV cache warm hits can dramatically reduce TTFT for repeated prefixes; we should test with cold and warmed cache profiles.
[03:12] Liam O'Neill: network is also a factor - we have customers in eu and us-west; want to understand cross-region routing and egress. our current infra has 1-2ms network latency to our cloud infra.
[03:22] Jordan Lee: for measurement we record RTT at client, ingress time at our edge, time at model container (start of inference), time to first token, and subsequent per-token deltas. Redwood can provide tracing hooks and per-route token breakdown in the console.
[03:34] Sofia Park: what about p95 vs p99 tradeoffs? product wants tight p95 but ops worried about p99 spikes.
[03:41] Priya Kapoor: typically you pick a primary SLO (TTFT p95) and a safety SLO (TTFT p99) - for example p95 < 200ms and p99 < 450ms. if p99 breaches we look at root cause: queueing, cold cache, noisy neighbor, or long sequence lengths.
[03:54] Ethan Morales: can you show examples of the benchmark report?
[03:57] Jordan Lee: yes we'll send last week's synthetic report as an example; it shows p50/p95/p99 TTFT and TPOT across batch sizes and model variants and a breakdown of time spent in kernel vs scheduling vs network.
[04:09] Maya Chen: for the POC length how long do you recommend?
[04:12] Priya Kapoor: our standard is 4 weeks: week 0 (kickoff & data collection), week 1 (synthetic baselines + config sweep), week 2 (production shadowing and tuning), week 3-4 (canary/reserved pilot & final report). extendable if you want a longer pilot.
[04:28] Jordan Lee: success criteria proposal from Redwood perspective (we wrote on the fly):
[04:31] Jordan Lee: a) TTFT p95 <= 200ms on chosen model variant under expected QPS profile, b) TPOT p95 <= 15ms for streaming token cost target, c) stable p99 within agreed threshold (<= 450ms) during 1hr peak window, d) cost-per-1000-tokens within agreed budget targets using batching/quantization recommendations.
[04:54] Ethan Morales: we want to be conservative: propose TTFT p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 500ms, and TPOT p95 <=20ms. if you can meet that, ops and product are happy.
[05:05] Priya Kapoor: sounds good - we will test both single-tenant dedicated pool and shared hosted variant to compare economics and tail behavior.
[05:12] Maya Chen: question: how do you simulate KV cache warmup? we have a lot of repeated prefixes for code completion.
[05:18] Priya Kapoor: we run two phases: cold-start (unique prefixes) and warmed (replay user prefixes to generate cache hits), and measure delta in TTFT; also measure hit rate vs throughput.
[05:28] Liam O'Neill: another infra constraint: we require SSO + private VPC peering for POC. does Redwood support that for Dedicated?
[05:36] Jordan Lee: yes Dedicated supports VPC peering, SAML SSO, KMS integrations - we'll include security artifacts in the follow-up packet.
[05:43] Sofia Park: any concerns about noisy neighbors or multi-tenant jitter?
[05:46] Priya Kapoor: for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated GPU pools; shared hosted can be fine but tail behavior can vary. Redwood supports autoscaling and isolation knobs; we'll measure noise in the pilot.
[05:57] Ethan Morales: what tools will you use to generate load? we currently use Locust internally.
[06:00] Priya Kapoor: we can reuse your Locust scripts, or provide our Redwood harness. we also capture tracing spans in both systems to correlate spikes.
[06:08] Jordan Lee: timeline recap: customer provides prompt set and traffic profile by 2027-05-09; Redwood runs synthetic benchmarks and returns report by 2027-05-13; schedule benchmark review week of 2027-05-17; start dedicated pilot week of 2027-05-24 pending SOW.
[06:22] Maya Chen: is there any recommended tuning knobs you'd want us to try during synthetic runs?
[06:26] Priya Kapoor: yes: quantization mode (int8 vs int4 if available), kv cache settings, batching window (10/20/50ms), prefilling cache on warm runs, and model parallel vs sharded configs. also look at compilation settings and kernel selection - Redwood runtime will auto-select but we can surface recommendations.
[06:43] Ethan Morales: ok good. on measurement, how do you compute TPOT p95? per-token delta averaged per-request or global token stream?
[06:49] Priya Kapoor: we compute per-token deltas per request and then aggregate across tokens to get p50/p95/p99. we also report per-request average token latency to see long tail effects of very long outputs.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: one more note: for short responses TTFT dominates perceived latency, so we will prioritize TTFT tuning for this POC.
[07:04] Sofia Park: any legal/compliance asks for pilot?
[07:07] Jordan Lee: we'll include SOC 2 and data handling docs; Dedicated POC can be set to not retain payloads beyond the pilot window.
[07:14] Ethan Morales: ok final question: how will we validate that the p99 we observed in synthetic test is reflective of prod? we've seen synthetic under-estimate tails.
[07:22] Priya Kapoor: that's why the production shadowing step is crucial - we mirror real requests to Redwood endpoints and tag them; that gives real tail without affecting users. also we'll measure distribution of sequence lengths and burst patterns to mimic them in synthetic runs.
[07:36] Maya Chen: ok that sounds comprehensive.
[07:38] Jordan Lee: recap of next steps - items in the notes and we'll share the sample benchmark report and the security packet. any other questions?
[07:45] Ethan Morales: no, thanks. appreciate the clarity.
[07:47] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:50] (end)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and small transcription errors; speakers frequently abbreviated names. Referenced artifacts: link to Redwood sample benchmark report (shared in chat), security packet (SOC2, SAML, KMS), Locust scripts (to be shared).
